cases.description: A source stating only the language leaves the bare form 'tsp' unresolved.
A source stating no locale leaves the bare form 'tsp' unresolved.
A source stating only the language leaves the bare form 'tsp.' unresolved.
A source stating no locale leaves the bare form 'tsp.' unresolved.
A source stating only the language leaves the bare form 'teaspoon' unresolved.
A source stating no locale leaves the bare form 'teaspoon' unresolved.
A source stating only the language leaves the bare form 'teaspoons' unresolved.
A source stating no locale leaves the bare form 'teaspoons' unresolved.
An English regional locale with no teaspoon alias set of its own does not acquire a metric teaspoon by falling back to the language level.
Removing the bare teaspoon forms does not disable language-level lookup: a gram still resolves through the `en` alias set from an `en-CA` source.
The United States regional identity is unchanged.
The Australian regional identity is unchanged.
An explicitly qualified metric teaspoon keeps its meaning in a United States source: the qualifier is matched before the region has anything unqualified to answer.
The qualified form is unaffected by the alias removal under `en`.
A locale-free source leaves the cup and the teaspoon of one line equally unresolved, which is the asymmetry registry 0.2.0 removes.
One ingredient convention resolves every term of a compound amount, including a teaspoon the reader was never asked about.
An occurrence interpretation settles the occurrence it addresses and nothing else; the remaining term stays available for review.
cases.source_text: 1 tablespoon plus 2 teaspoons neutral oil, reviewed one measure at a time

cases.description: With no answer at all, no convention is invented from the ingredient.
cases.source_text: 1 tablespoon plus 2 teaspoons neutral oil, unreviewed

cases.description: A German source resolves TL to the metric culinary teaspoon through its language-level alias, and the gram keeps its own identity. This is the answer a convention has to outrank.

An ingredient convention outranks a language-level alias match: the same German TL resolves to the US customary teaspoon under the decision. The gram is untouched because the profile does not cover it.
An ingredient convention outranks an exact-region locale match. The difference from the stated locale is a review disclosure, not agreement.
An explicitly qualified metric teaspoon keeps its authored meaning while the unqualified tablespoon of the same ingredient follows the decision.
cases.source_text: 1 tablespoon plus 2 metric teaspoons neutral oil

cases.description: An occurrence interpretation outranks the ingredient convention for the occurrence it addresses, which is how a reviewed exception is expressed.
A convention that maps no cup leaves the cup unresolved rather than borrowing another convention to complete the ingredient.
A convention reaches every alternative branch. The unambiguous gram branch is untouched, and the two amounts are not reconciled.
The authored alternatives disagree materially under the decided interpretation. Both source assertions survive resolution unchanged.
A convention submitted for one ingredient leaves the identical alias in another ingredient of the same recipe unresolved.
One ingredient can contain the same alias twice. An occurrence identity distinguishes them; an alias string could not.
cases.source_text: 1 cup water, plus 1 cup for the glaze

cases.description: Two incompatible interpretations of one occurrence are a conflict, not a race between the first and the last answer.
Two incompatible conventions for one ingredient scope are a conflict, and must not fall back to the locale the source stated.
A metric culinary profile names the identities it selects. It is not derived from a unit whose factor happens to agree with another.
The ingredient whose only measure is a teaspoon is resolvable by decision once the bare form no longer resolves at the language level.
An uncovered convention-dependent family stays unresolved inside a convention scope. Falling through to the source locale produced a US customary tablespoon beside a metric teaspoon on one line.
cases.source_text: 1 tablespoon plus 2 teaspoons neutral oil, read as metric

cases.description: The same rule under an exact regional locale that would have answered. The locale is evidence about the document, not a definition of a measure the person has said to read another way.
cases.source_text: 2 tablespoons golden syrup, read as metric

cases.description: Resolver level: an occurrence that already carries the identity its qualifier states keeps it inside the same scope. The ingredient-line corpus tests that the phrase is recognized from the text.
cases.source_text: 1 Australian tablespoon plus 2 teaspoons oil, read as metric

cases.description: An occurrence interpretation settles a measure the convention cannot, which is how a partly covered profile is completed rather than abandoned.
cases.source_text: 1 tablespoon plus 2 teaspoons oil, mostly metric

cases.description: The rule bites only on a contested family. A gram is metric and nothing else is called a gram, so a convention that says nothing about mass leaves it resolving exactly as it did.
cases.source_text: 1 cup flour and 200 grams flour, read as metric

cases.description: A German EL resolves to the metric culinary tablespoon by language. A US customary decision for the ingredient outranks that alias.
Single-letter T and t are case-sensitive US aliases and name different units.
A case-insensitive word alias matches under any capitalisation of its letters.
The case-insensitive ml set admits ML and Ml beside the case-sensitive mL set. Matching is tolerant, not strict SI or UCUM parsing.
